newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weekend of European trucking disruption expected.
newsitem.headline: Weekend of European trucking disruption expected.

text.p: The German transport workers union OeTV said it has called a day of action by truck and bus drivers on Monday June 9 in what promises to be a long weekend of disputes hitting the trucking industry across Europe.
The German protests over long hours were part of a Europe-wide day of action organised by the International Transport Workers Federation (ITF), the union said.
Protests lasting several hours were planned on the borders with France at Strasbourg, with Poland at Frankfurt/Oder and with the Czech Republic, a statement said.
Action was also expected at the port of Rostock and at locations across Germany.

The OeTV said it wanted European drivers to have a maximum 12 hour day instead of a maximum 10 hour driving time with breaks which they were regularly forced to ignore to meet deadlines and unregulated waiting and loading times.
"Three hundred to 400 working hours a month are not rare. The pitiless competitive fight in freight and passenger transport is borne on the backs of the employees," the union added.
In the UK the Freight Transport Association (FTA) has warned its members of the ITF dispute but said the threat seems to have diminished following the election of a socialist French government.
The FTA said that the disruption was expected to take the form of demonstrations, but more extensive unofficial action could not be ruled out.

The FTA listed other disputes as the closure today (Friday) of the French-Spanish border by Spanish farmers and lorry drivers who are retaliating against French attacks on Spanish lorries carrying fuit and vegetables; a blockade on Friday and Saturday in Slovakia by striking public transport workers; road closures in Slovenia affecting lorries on Friday and Saturday (June 6 and 7).

However, Irish hauliers who were blockading two Irish ports in a pay dispute with shipping companies agreed on Friday to lift their blockade pending talks with the shipping firms and Irish transport minister Alan Dukes.
The hauliers had been blocking traffic in Dublin docks since earlier this week and extended the protest to Rosslare, on the southwest coast, on Friday morning.
